title: Build closures that remember the values they were made with

blocks.text: A lambda that reads a variable from the method that created it **closes over** that variable: it carries the value with it after the method has returned. That makes small factories possible, each returning a function tuned by its arguments.

items: `multiplier(int factor)` returns a `Function<Integer, Integer>` that multiplies its input by `factor`.
`between(int min, int max)` returns a `Predicate<Integer>` that tests whether a value lies in the range from `min` to `max`, both included. When `min` is greater than `max` the range is empty.

`prefixFilter(String prefix, int minLength)` returns a `Function<List<String>, List<String>>` that keeps, in order and duplicates included, every word that starts with `prefix` (case-sensitive, as `String.startsWith` decides) and is at least `minLength` long.

blocks.text: Check the ends of the range, and make sure several functions made by the same factory do not interfere with one another.

cases.says: The multiplier multiplies by the factor it was made with.
The range check accepts values inside the range and rejects values outside it.
The filter keeps only words with the prefix and at least the minimum length.
Both ends of the range belong to it.
Two multipliers made with different factors each keep their own factor.

concepts: A lambda closes over the values it reads, so each function made by a factory keeps its own values.
